basis: Craniofacial and limb skeletal malformations define this umbrella; other organ abnormalities vary by subtype.
Arenavirus infection; neurologic disease, hemorrhage and visceral injury vary across infections and are not universal defining organ involvement.
Acute inflammation of the larynx and pharynx, ordinarily caused by respiratory infection.
Tumour originates in the uterine cervix, outside the axes; skeletal muscle differentiation does not establish skeletal muscle involvement.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and cerebral atrophy define the disorder; other findings are minor dysmorphism or below 30%.
Persistent inward ocular misalignment affects binocular visual function.
Residual open-angle glaucoma represents established glaucomatous ocular and optic nerve damage.
Epilepsy, intellectual disability and IgA deficiency define it; short fifth finger 80–99%, dental abnormalities 30–79%; conjunctival telangiectasia lacks demonstrated ocular dysfunction.
Motor neuron degeneration defines ALS; established skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 5/10 patients. Respiratory failure occurs in only 1/10.
Abnormally reduced brain growth defines this neurodevelopmental disorder; extracerebral involvement depends on the underlying syndrome.
Genetic neonatal bile duct disease causes fibrosis and liver failure; reported urinary abnormality is 25%; splenomegaly reflects portal hypertension.
Malignant tumour originates in the adrenal medulla, an endocrine gland compartment.
Polydactyly is defining; urinary malformations and hydronephrosis occur in 30–79%. Reproductive abnormalities lack an axis; cardiac and intestinal defects are usually under 30%.
Parkinsonism and intellectual disability define the disorder; persistent strabismus affects ocular alignment in 30–79%.
Pancreatic endocrine tumour producing gastrin; acid-peptic disease belongs to an associated functional syndrome and is not intrinsic to every tumour.
Isolated forearm skeletal dysplasia with ulnar hypoplasia and radial bowing.
Muscular dystrophy and joint contractures define it; esotropia occurs in 30–79%. Respiratory failure reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Tight, inelastic facial skin and blepharophimosis characterize the syndrome; minor skeletal and ear dysmorphism alone does not establish functional organ damage.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and progressive visual loss are common, exceeding 30% in childhood CLN6 disease.
Hereditary photodermatosis causing cutaneous UV sensitivity, freckling and skin changes; DNA repair dysfunction does not itself imply a metabolic axis.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation directly injures lung tissue; blood eosinophilia alone is not a blood-cell disease.
Inborn glycerol metabolism defect causes metabolic crises; episodic vomiting and altered consciousness do not establish persistent gastrointestinal or neurologic damage.
Carcinoma originates in the subglottic laryngeal airway.
Developmental impairment and skeletal/digital malformations characterize distal 4q deletion; congenital heart defects occur in roughly 50%, cleft palate in roughly 30%; deletion size varies.
Intellectual disability and pronounced arachnodactyly define the syndrome; genital abnormalities lack an axis, and facial appearance alone adds no damaged organ.
